A waitlist landing page for Margin, a quiet note-taking app for researchers and writers. Calm, literary and confident. A large editorial serif headline set left, "Notes that remember what you were thinking", a one-line subhead, and a single email field with a "Join the waitlist" call-to-action button beside it. To the right, a cropped real screenshot of the note editor showing a linked note and a margin comment. Below the fold, three short reasons laid out in an asymmetric row (not identical cards), then a footer with the company name. Warm off-white paper background, ink-black text, one muted terracotta accent used only on the button. Serif headings, clean humanist sans for body. Generous whitespace, no gradients, no stock icons.

A pricing page for Relay, a team chat tool for small engineering teams. Clear, trustworthy and slightly playful. A short header with the logo and Sign in, a headline "Pay for the team you have", and a monthly/yearly toggle. Three plans side by side: Free, Team ($8 per user) and Business ($15 per user), with Team highlighted as most popular through a stronger border and filled button rather than a badge. Each plan lists five concrete features with check marks. Under the plans, a feature comparison table with grouped rows (Messaging, Integrations, Security), then a two-column FAQ with six real questions. Neutral warm grey background, near-black text, a confident cobalt primary. Geometric sans throughout, tabular numbers for prices.

A documentation page for the Forge CLI, titled "Install Forge". Precise, calm and highly readable, like the best developer docs. A top bar with the product name, a search field showing a keyboard shortcut hint and a version switcher. A left sidebar navigation with grouped sections (Getting started, Guides, Reference) and the current page highlighted. The main column has a short intro paragraph, tabbed install instructions for macOS, Linux and Windows with copyable code blocks (brew install forge, curl script, winget), a callout box warning about PATH setup, a numbered "Verify your install" step with terminal output, and Previous/Next links at the bottom. A right-hand "On this page" table of contents. Light theme: white background, slate text, one teal accent for links and the active nav item. Sans serif for prose, monospace for code.

An analytics dashboard for Northwind, a subscription coffee roaster, used by the operations lead every morning. Dense but calm and precise. A collapsible left sidebar with navigation (Overview, Subscriptions, Orders, Customers, Settings) and the workspace switcher. A top bar with a date range picker (Last 30 days), a compare-to-previous toggle and an export button. A row of four KPI tiles: Monthly recurring revenue $48,210 (+6.2%), Active subscribers 3,912, Churn 2.1%, Average order value $31.40, each with a small sparkline. Below, a large line chart of revenue by week with a dashed previous-period line, next to a donut of subscriptions by plan. At the bottom, a sortable orders table with status pills (Paid, Shipped, Refunded), customer names, totals and a row action menu, plus pagination. Off-white background, charcoal text, a deep green primary and a muted amber for warnings. Tabular figures everywhere.

A project management workspace for Atlas, used by a product team planning a launch. Sophisticated, focused and information-rich without clutter. A narrow left rail with workspace and project icons, then a project sidebar listing views (Board, List, Timeline, Docs). The main area is a kanban board with four columns (Backlog, In progress, In review, Done), each with a count and an add button; cards show a title, an assignee avatar, a due date, a priority marker and subtask progress, and one card is being dragged with a drop placeholder. A filter bar above the board with chips for assignee, label and sprint, plus a search field. On the right, an open task detail side panel for "Write launch announcement": status and priority selectors, assignee, due date, a description with a checklist, an activity feed with two comments and a mention, and a comment composer at the bottom. Light neutral UI with a single violet accent, crisp 1px borders instead of shadows, compact 13px text, clear empty and hover states.

A sign-in screen for Bloom, a plant care app. Friendly, calm and uncluttered. The app logo mark and name at the top, a short welcoming headline "Welcome back", email and password fields with clear labels, a show/hide password toggle, a "Forgot password?" link, a full-width primary "Sign in" button, a divider with "or", and buttons for Continue with Apple and Continue with Google. At the bottom, "New here? Create an account". Soft sage green primary on a warm cream background, dark green-grey text, rounded but not bubbly shapes, a friendly sans serif. Respect the iOS safe areas and 44pt touch targets.

The home screen of Streak, a habit tracker for people building small daily routines. Encouraging, clean and tactile. A greeting with today's date at the top and a weekly calendar strip with today selected. A progress ring showing 3 of 5 habits done today. A list of today's habits (Drink water 6/8 glasses, Read 20 minutes, Stretch, Journal, No phone after 10pm), each with an icon, a short streak count and a large tap-to-complete check. A floating add button and a bottom tab bar (Today, Stats, Habits, Profile). Off-white background, deep navy text, a warm coral accent for completed states. Rounded geometric sans, generous spacing.

A restaurant menu screen in Harvest, a local food delivery app. Appetizing, warm and easy to scan. A hero photo of the restaurant "Lotus Kitchen" with a back button and a favourite button, then the name, cuisine (Thai), rating 4.7 with 1.2k reviews, delivery time 25-35 min and fee. A sticky horizontal category tab bar (Popular, Starters, Curries, Noodles, Drinks). Menu items as rows with dish name, a one-line description, price and a square food photo with an add button; one item already has a quantity stepper. A sticky bottom cart bar showing 3 items and $38.50 with a View cart button. Cream background, near-black text, a saffron orange primary. Clear type hierarchy, real dish names.

The home screen of Ledger, a personal finance app for young professionals. Premium, calm and trustworthy. A header with the user's avatar and a notifications bell. A total balance card ($12,480.22 across accounts) with a small show/hide toggle and an up arrow showing +$340 this month. Quick actions as a row of four (Send, Request, Top up, More). A horizontal carousel of two cards (a debit card and a savings pot at 62% of its goal). A spending this month section with a compact bar chart by category. A recent transactions list grouped by day with merchant logos, categories and amounts, income in green. A bottom tab bar (Home, Cards, Insights, Profile). Dark theme: near-black background, soft white text, one electric lime accent used sparingly. Tabular numbers.

A group conversation screen in Thread, a messaging app for close friends. Lively, personal and modern. A header with the group name "Lisbon trip", stacked member avatars, and call and info buttons. The conversation shows a day separator, incoming and outgoing message bubbles with grouped consecutive messages, a reply quoting an earlier message, emoji reactions under a bubble, a photo grid attachment, a voice note with waveform and duration, a shared location card, read receipts, and a typing indicator. A composer at the bottom with an attach button, a text field, an emoji button and a send/mic button, sitting above the keyboard safe area. Light theme with a soft blue-grey background, white incoming bubbles and indigo outgoing bubbles, a clean sans serif.
